title: Deleting a user keeps their articles and sets author_id to NULL.
content:
The articles.author_id foreign key uses ondelete SET NULL. Comments, favorites and follows referencing users use CASCADE instead.
Source: app/app/db/migrations/versions/fdf8821871d7_main_tables.py:108

title: Article lists default to 20 items with a minimum of 1 and no maximum limit.
content:
ArticlesFilters declares limit with default DEFAULT_ARTICLES_LIMIT (20) and ge=1 only. Offset defaults to 0 with ge=0, and no upper bound is set on limit.
Source: app/app/models/schemas/articles.py:42

title: articlesCount in list responses is the length of the returned page, not the total match count.
content:
list_articles sets articles_count to len(articles) after applying limit and offset. Clients cannot read the total number of matching articles from this field.
Source: app/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:49

title: Invalid or unresolvable tokens are rejected with 403, not 401.
content:
_get_current_user maps a token decode error and a missing user to HTTP 403 with MALFORMED_PAYLOAD. The wrong prefix case in the same module also returns 403.
Source: app/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py:90

title: The Authorization header must use the prefix Token, not Bearer.
content:
Settings default jwt_token_prefix to Token. The auth dependency splits the header on a space and rejects any other prefix with 403 WRONG_TOKEN_PREFIX.
Source: app/app/core/settings/app.py:29

title: API models expose snake_case fields as camelCase JSON aliases.
content:
RWModel sets alias_generator to convert_field_to_camel_case and allow_population_by_field_name. Datetimes are serialized as UTC ISO strings ending in Z.
Source: app/app/models/domain/rwmodel.py:21

title: The asyncpg connection pool defaults to a fixed size of 10 connections.
content:
AppSettings sets both max_connection_count and min_connection_count to 10. connect_to_db passes them as min_size and max_size to asyncpg.create_pool.
Source: app/app/core/settings/app.py:22

title: Access tokens expire one week after issue.
content:
ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES is 60 * 24 * 7 and create_access_token_for_user passes it as the expiry delta. There is no refresh token flow in the code.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:12

title: Access tokens are signed with the symmetric HS256 algorithm.
content:
The JWT service sets ALGORITHM to HS256 and uses it both to encode tokens and as the only accepted algorithm when decoding. The same secret_key signs and verifies tokens.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:11

title: The access token identifies the user by username, not by id.
content:
The token payload is JWTUser(username=...), and _get_current_user looks the user up with get_user_by_username. Because update_user can change the username, an old token stops resolving to a user after a rename.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:29

title: Login returns the same 400 error for an unknown email and a wrong password.
content:
The login route builds one wrong_login_error with INCORRECT_LOGIN_INPUT and raises it in both failure branches. The response does not reveal which part was wrong.
Source: app/app/api/routes/authentication.py:30

title: Article ownership is checked by comparing author username with the current user's username.
content:
check_user_can_modify_article returns article.author.username == user.username. Update and delete routes depend on this check and return 403 when it fails.
Source: app/app/services/articles.py:23

title: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt through a passlib CryptContext.
content:
pwd_context is a passlib CryptContext with schemes bcrypt and deprecated auto. verify_password and get_password_hash both go through it.
Source: app/app/services/security.py:4

title: A separate per-user salt is stored and prepended to the password before bcrypt hashing.
content:
change_password generates a new salt, stores it in users.salt, and hashes salt + password. check_password must prepend the same stored salt, so the salt column and the hash must change together.
Source: app/app/models/domain/users.py:24

title: Database access uses raw SQL files loaded with aiosql on asyncpg, not an ORM.
content:
queries is built by aiosql.from_path over the sql folder with the asyncpg driver. Repositories call named query functions on this object.
Source: app/app/db/queries/queries.py:5

title: An article slug is derived from its title with slugify and must be unique.
content:
get_slug_for_article returns slugify(title). The create route rejects a new article with 400 ARTICLE_ALREADY_EXISTS when that slug exists, and the articles.slug column is unique.
Source: app/app/services/articles.py:19

title: Changing an article title regenerates its slug, so its URL changes.
content:
update_article_by_slug computes a new slug from the new title when a title is given. The update route does not run the duplicate slug check that create runs.
Source: app/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:100

title: updated_at is maintained by a Postgres trigger, not by application code.
content:
The migration creates update_updated_at_column, which sets NEW.updated_at = now(), and attaches it BEFORE UPDATE on users, articles and commentaries. Tables added later need the same trigger.
Source: app/app/db/migrations/versions/fdf8821871d7_main_tables.py:27
